No gate code shall change in this record.
payload.description:
## Context
When the decomposer and the agents cut work, I want units of about one agent-session day, so I can stop small records and ledger-only commits from inflating the history. Owner, 2026-11-13: "the stories seem to small for current models, i think a 1-day of work cut is better than these small chungs, which only inflate the git history with many commits."
Measured in the orchestrator's research (local file research-story-size.md, 2026-11-13): 119 of 258 commits in 14 days change only the ledger, about 110 of them written by sessions; 29 of 45 code records closed under 1 hour (median 0.39 h); median 8 records per day, 31 on 2026-11-12. Causes: the size=small fast path with split anything larger (GUIDANCE.md:182, process_evidence.py:224-225); the decomposer has an upper bound and no target or lower bound (decomposer/agent.yaml:22-29, :55-56; decompose-plan/skill.yaml:17); harness-loop/references/operations.md:217 asks for ledger commits between steps, against work-tracker/skill.yaml:31 and unneeded since merge.py:673-675 commits ledger dirt at landing; release-fragments asks one fragment per record although release.py:197-198 credits every id a fragment names; decider/agent.yaml:38 describes a diff-size downgrade that classify.py:36 and integrity.py:170 never apply. Proposals 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 of that file.
Owner question, not decided here: the working-set band ceiling of 331,200 tokens (config.py:245) is the only size refusal. Measured 2026-11-13 with read_cost.scope_read_cost: src/basicly/cli.py prices 4000 tokens in the band (SCOPE_FILE_READ_CAP), 53,120 uncapped; four large engine files price 16,000. So one wide file does not reach the ceiling; a scope of more than about 80 large files would.
Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13. Builder: codex-1 as Text cut 2, together with the audit skill part B; do not claim it here.
payload.title: Text cut 2: size work units at about one agent-session day

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When basicly worktree merge runs with a dry-run flag, it shall list every refusal the landing would meet, each with its fixing command, and change nothing.
When the dry run lists no refusal, a real landing of the same lane and destination shall not refuse for any of the listed causes.
payload.description:
## Context
When a lane is about to land, I want one command that lists every refusal the landing would meet, so I can fix them all before one full verify instead of meeting them one at a time.
Evidence 2026-11-13 on basicly-gtb19bg.43.37 and basicly-f2zwd26: refusals arrived one per attempt: dirty manifest timestamp, missing Lefthook artifact in a new worktree, unverified destination, missing confirmation evidence, a merge commit in the lane (REBASE-MERGE-COMMIT), an unknown worktree session, and an engine change that needs the candidate engine. Each retry repeated a full verify of about 8 minutes. Measured (orchestrator research, .basicly/usage/landing-timings.json): 10 of 16 landing attempts since 2026-10-30 did not land: 4 not-ready, 3 verify-failed, 3 rebase-merge-commit. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13. Build after the vault cutover (.43.34).
payload.title: Let a dry-run landing list every refusal at once

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When basicly worktree merge names several record ids, it shall check the confirmation evidence of each and refuse by name for every id that lacks it.
When such a landing merges, the merge commit shall name every id, and the destination verification marker shall cover every id.
payload.description:
## Context
When one lane carries several records, I want the landing to name all of them, check each one's confirmation evidence and mark the destination for all, so I can land a day-size cut once.
Today basicly worktree merge takes one --bead (merge.py:599-608); the landing guard and the confirmation check run for that id only (merge.py:614); the other records need a manual review, confirm and close. What exists already (orchestrator research 2026-11-13): lane sub-tasks with a cap of 10 (loop.py:1253-1260, config.py:262) and multi-id commit subjects (message-format.md:33). Still missing: several ids on worktree merge, a confirmation check per id, and one destination marker for all ids. Landing statistic: 10 of 16 landing attempts since 2026-10-30 did not land. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13. Build after the vault cutover (.43.34).
payload.title: Let one landing name every record of a cut

payload.acceptance_criteria: When a test reads a BASICLY_ or BR_ environment variable that conftest does not clear or set, a check shall name the test and the variable.
payload.description:
## Context
When a test runs in an agent session, I want it independent of the session's environment, so I can trust a local full verify.
Evidence 2026-11-13: three tests read the ambient BASICLY_HOLDER and failed on main with BASICLY_HOLDER=codex-1 and passed without it; codex-1 fixed it by adding BASICLY_HOLDER to WRITER_MARKERS in tests/conftest.py:41 (basicly-e4t2txx). Other variables can do the same. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13. No build now.
payload.title: Refuse a test that reads an undeclared BASICLY or BR environment variable

payload.acceptance_criteria: When the test runs 10 times beside a parallel full suite, the count of failures shall be on this record, and a failure caused only by CPU starvation shall be refused by name rather than counted as a claim defect.
payload.description:
## Context
When several suites run on one machine, I want test_a_small_real_load_makes_claims_in_every_session_and_one_holder_per_record to pass or fail only on claim behaviour, so I can trust a full verify under load.
Evidence 2026-11-13: during a full run under load (load averages 3.31, 5.11, 6.69 at 12:23:33 UTC) it dumped a faulthandler timeout at .scripts/claim_load.py:188 with no FAILED record. The 60 s dump comes from faulthandler_timeout in pyproject.toml:61 and does not fail the test. The risk is in its assertions sessions_without_claims == 0 and claims >= 4, which depend on CPU time (claim_load.Config sessions=4, machines=2, scale=8, minutes=8, seed=3); exit 3 (foreign CPU) is accepted. Not measured. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13. No build now.
payload.title: Keep the small claim-load test from failing under machine load

payload.text: Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13: (1) Codex agents claim, commit the ledger on main, then run basicly worktree create. (2) basicly-e4t2txx stays closed; codex-1 followed work-tracker write.md (close before the resolving commit). (3) I run the destination verify for basicly-e4t2txx before my next landing; following the landing gate over AGENTS.md line 59 was right, the contradiction lives on basicly-oov1ouu, neither rule changes today; basicly-oov1ouu moves up, no build now; basicly-i665i0o accepted. (4) Five day-size cuts: A = .43.36 + .43.38; B = .43.30 + .43.39 + .43.40 before the rehearsal; C = basicly-ak6qrz0 + .43.41 + the burst joined-wait bound, parallel to B after a file-overlap check; D = .43.33 rehearsal; E = .43.34 cutover alone. One landing per cut, per-record review, confirmation and close. (5) Ledger commits only at the end of a cut or when another session must see a claim; the landing tool commits ledger dirt itself (merge.py:672-674). (6) Lock guards a landing or a release only. Records filed 2026-11-13: basicly-azz4whe (Text cut 1), basicly-eb4923k (Text cut 2, day-size units), basicly-9qau67d (dry-run landing), basicly-ojkqgbg (multi-record landing), basicly-nl03zgh (ambient env in tests), basicly-pl4ybu0 (claim-load under load).

Review and decisions, 2026-11-13. Decided by the orchestrator: the reader defect in a repository without a ledger folder is part of this slice; cut A moves to lane cut-a (from main 391897a1) because m5-v4c forks from ccca60bb and never ran against .43.37. Commits on cut-a (cherry-picked, no merge commit): 3fa9782b lane work, 0c4ad31e seed fix, bec2531c reader fallback, a764a19b Target prefix default. Seed fix: test_a_claimed_record_mints_past_the_view_holder_line_without_a_gap fails without it (view totals.events 3 against minted 4; after the test correction an exact field repeat was not seen as a repeat). The lane's original assertion expected a status repeat after a comment to be dropped, which a plain ledger also lands; the test now repeats one field draft. Reader fallback: test_the_board_graph_gate_and_label_readers_read_no_ledger_folder_as_empty fails without it with LedgerMissingError; one helper owned_store.readable_ledger serves all readers. Integration fault found by moving onto main: the lane made prefix a required sixth field of vault_write.Target, main's vault_cli _unassign_vault builds it with five, so unassign through the vault would have raised TypeError after the landing. Tests: 4474 passed on cut-a against main 391897a1. Open: VaultUnreadError has no test; readers that catch TrackerDivergenceError show an unreadable vault as empty; kit blocked, stats and dor read the local ledger; engine create bypasses the vault; two writes before a share mint the same seq.
